characteristics.cultivar: Individual Dan Cong old bushes with 'honey orchid' aroma profile

description.short: One of the most popular aroma types of Phoenix Dan Cong with a pronounced honey-floral fragrance
description.overview: Dan Cong translates to 'single bush' — historically, each tree on Phoenix Mountain was harvested and processed individually, yielding dozens of distinct aromatic profiles. Mi Lan Xiang ('Honey Orchid Aroma') is the most famous among them.
description.leaf: Long, twisted dark brown leaves with undulating edges
description.aroma: Honey, orchid, ripe fruit — an intense and unmistakable floral-honey bouquet
description.taste: Sweet, floral, with a full body and a subtle mountain minerality
description.aftertaste: Long sweet finish with a lingering return of honeyed fragrance
description.processing: Harvesting from individual trees → sun withering → multiple shaking sessions for edge oxidation (a hallmark of Dan Cong is very vigorous shaking) → kill-green → rolling into long strips (not balls) → baking/roasting

history.origin: The name 'Dan Cong' reflects the tradition of processing leaves from each tree separately without blending them with leaves from other trees — a rare practice in Chinese tea production.
history.development: Many tea trees on Phoenix Mountain are believed to trace their lineage back to the Southern Song dynasty and are several centuries old; the aroma subtypes (xiangxing) evolved over centuries through natural selection and clonal propagation via cuttings.
history.modern: Today there are more than ten recognized Dan Cong aroma types (Mi Lan Xiang, Ya Shi Xiang, Zhi Lan Xiang, and others), each originating from a distinct tree lineage.
interestingFacts: Individual ancient trees several hundred years old still survive on Phoenix Mountain; tea harvested from them is exceptionally rare and prized.
Unlike many oolongs rolled into tight spheres like Tie Guan Yin, Dan Cong is twisted into long, slender strips.
